title: Bloom, early and full

reference.grammar: One bloom printed through a green dot screen, early and full.

techniques.name: Dot-screen bloom

pitch.label: Dot pitch
pitch.note: Spacing of the three dot screens the blooms are printed in, as a multiple of the page’s 1.85 px. Larger is coarser.

sangle.label: Screen angle
sangle.note: Turn of all three screens together, added to their own 15°, 45° and 75°.

shape.label: Dot
shape.note: The screen’s dot: round, or a square of the same area.

gain.label: Dot gain
gain.note: How far each dot spreads for the tone it carries, as a multiple of the page’s own. Above 1 the screens close into solid.

misreg.label: Misregistration
misreg.note: How far the sky and black screens slip off the cobalt one, as a multiple of the page’s own (4 and 1.5 units).

techniques.implementation: A scatter of marks is printed through a coarse dot screen; dot size carries the density, so the bloom fades at its edge without a gradient. Drawn by the source page’s own code on a clock this plate drives; its strokes, marks, inks and type pass through the dials.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.

techniques.name: Justified plate
techniques.implementation: Figures keep their proportions and share a row height; each row fills the plate width. Every split of the figures into rows is tried, and the one whose row heights sit closest to the target wins.

pass_order: read · points measured from each figure
